newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European bourses down, ignore Wall St boom.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European bourses down, ignore Wall St boom.

text.p: European stocks mostly fell on Thursday, with investors distracted by interest rate worries and ignoring Wall Street which hit another record overnight, the 10th this month.
On currency markets, the dollar was firm against the mark and climbed half a yen after Japanese authorities shut down a troubled bank, the first time they have done so in five decades.

Gloomy European markets drew no comfort from the bull run in in New York. The Dow Jones average closed at 6,430.02 points on Wednesday, beating the record of the previous day and chalking up the 41st peak this year.

Domestic issues depressed bourses on this side of the Atlantic, "decoupling" them from the New York rally, which was driven by gains in General Motors shares. Europe frequently runs in parallel with Wall Street.

In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks slipped by 0.4 percent as the market became more preoccupied by sterling's strength, interest rates and the possibility of unwelcome news in next week's budget. Dealers said investors feared that finance minister Kenneth Clarke might indulge in pre-election tax cuts in next Tuesday's budget despite rising inflationary pressures.
"It would blow his credibility and the Bank of England would howl so I can't see it myself. But the uncertainty is enough to keep everyone flat in this market," another trader said.
Investors were still unsettled by British figures issued on Wednesday showing stronger-than-expected October retail sales and money supply growth, which re-ignited interest rate anxieties.

In Frankfurt, stocks slipped by nearly 0.5 percent in listless trading which dealers said lacked direction. Volumes in early computer trade were thin, with interest low even in newly-floated Deutsche Telekom shares.
Telekom was slightly down in early dealings, off 10 pfennigs at 31.90 marks, after the stock slipped in both New York and Tokyo, but some dealers said they saw profit taking coming to an end.

French shares slipped in and out of the minus column in early trade as the looming Friday monthly settlement outweighed New York's record high overnight close. "No one has really any desire to buy ahead of the settlement," said one trader.
Eurotunnel was down 0.67 percent, extending losses after Monday's Channel Tunnel fire. Eurotunnel announced that freight trains began running again early on Thursday.

The dollar was stronger against the yen but underlying support for the yen came from Japan's robust September diffusion index of leading indicators which showed the Japanese economy was continuing to recover gradually.
"The leading indicator index was firmer...It should argue for a stronger yen," said Ros Lifton, senior international economist at HSBC markets.

Currency traders were also keeping a close eye on Japan's banking sector after the closure of Hanwa Bank Ltd, suffocating under 190 billion yen ($1.7 billion) in problem loans. But analysts were optimistic.
"It is really the tail end of the (banking) crisis in Japan and I don't think it is getting any deeper because operating profits for banks are improving," said one.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.72 yen and 1.4983 marks, compared with 111.17 yen and 1.4960 marks in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 10.4 points at 3,952.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 1.59 points at 2,234.92.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 12.46 points at 2,762.04.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $378.50 an ounce, compared to Wednesday's close of $379.15. Silver was down two cents at $4.94.
